newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- T-bonds may poke at highs before pullback.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- T-bonds may poke at highs before pullback.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures may try to edge up to new highs again before a widely anticipated correction, technical analysts said.

"I still think we have a little bit of a push higher near term to another new high," said Michael Zentz, Treasury market strategist at FX Concepts. "And then I think we're going to trade quietly off."
"We got some negative news today but they (T-bonds) managed to hold up," he said, noting that the market had weathered two waves of selloffs today to return to positive territory.
"It makes me think that there are strong bids out there," Zentz said, referring to the persistent buying on dips, a hallmark of a bull market.

September T-bond futures bounced back toward 115 in late morning trade after slipping in mid-morning on strong readings in the Philadelphia Fed's July business survey. Earlier, it had also bounced from overnight lows.
Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage, agreed that the current upward leg on the daily chart was likely to last another day or two.
He said the daily stochastic was hovering in overbought territory, with the 60-minute and 100-minute stochastics rising in "modestly overbought" territory.
Analysts said a correction was unavoidable eventually and would likely start in a few days.
But Grauer expected the pullback to be shallow, given the daily stochastic's recent tendency to cut short its down cycle.

"It looks like the pattern now is truncated reaction followed by up-thrust to new highs," he said. He noted that the two most recent daily stochastic cycles during the market's three-month rally has shown such behavior.
"That's what I expect to happen again -- the daily then powering us to 116 on the next round," he said. He projected 113-1/2 as the worst-case support for September T-bonds.
In ther longer term, Grauer added, the upcycle in the weekly stochastic had several more weeks to go, after which the market's steep upward trend channel would probably inflect to a flatter slope.
Still, the monthly stochastic has made a big turnaround in June, and since the monthly cycle typically lasted more than a year, a target of 120 now seemed realistic, he said.
He added that the percent K and D values of the monthly stochastic were still widening their positive spread this month after June's upcross.
